summary: Elizabeth Errington is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned a diploma from Johannesburg Art Foundation and a B.A. from SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar, later curating coins at the British Museum (1993) and advising Oxford's Gandhara Connections (~2016).

Elizabeth Guthrie is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury (~1999). Her career includes serving as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

Elizabeth J. Harris is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She completed her doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Kelaniya (~1988–1993) under Ananda Guruge and Y. Karunadasa, later holding a post at the University of Birmingham (~2019).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1969–1978) and held posts at the University of Washington (~1978–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).
Elizabeth Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. She has taught Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto (attested 2020).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, Paul Groner, and Ngawang Wangyal. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She served as Director at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006), supervised by Thomas B. Larsson, Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.
Ellen M. Raven is an Indologist and archaeologist. She held posts at Leiden University (attested 2003, 2018) and served on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies (attested 2018).

Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist who studied under P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1978–1979) and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania in 1998, supervised by George Cardona and Wilhelm Halbfass.

Elliot Sperling was a scholar of Tibetology and history. He studied at Queens College (B.A.) and Indiana University (M.A., Ph.D.) under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn Struve, later serving as an associate professor at Indiana University (1987–2015) and professor at Harvard (1992–1993).

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, where she was an associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He served as an editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1926) and held posts at the Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under MA supervisor John C. Huntington. She held posts at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education (1994–1996) and Ohio State (1999–2001).
Emil Krebs was a sinologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Breslau (~1887–1888) and the University of Berlin (~1888–1890) under Wilhelm Grube.

Emil Rödiger was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies who earned his Dr. phil. and Lic. theol. at the University of Halle. He served as professor of Oriental languages at Halle (1830–1860) and the University of Berlin (1860).

Emil Sieg was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from Berlin (1891) and studied at Munich, Tübingen, and Göttingen. He held professorships at the University of Berlin (1896–1908), Kiel University (1909–1919), and the University of Göttingen (1920).

Emilio Teza was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Anton Boller (~1855–1859). He worked at Biblioteca Marciana and the Laurentian Library, and held professorships at the Universities of Bologna (1860), Pisa (~1868–1886), and Padua (~1886–1912).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who completed degrees at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She held a post at the University of Colorado (~2003).
